text: Parallelograms which are on the same base and between the same parallels are equal to one another. Let $ABCD$ and $EBCF$ be parallelograms on the same base $BC$, and between the same parallels $AF$ and $BC$. I say that $ABCD$ is equal to parallelogram $EBCF$.
For since $ABCD$ is a parallelogram, $AD$ is equal to $BC$ [Prop.~1.34].
So, for the same (reasons), $EF$ is also equal to $BC$.
Thus, the whole (straight-line) $AE$ is equal to the whole (straight-line) $DF$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the whole (straight-line) $AE$ is equal to the whole (straight-line) $DF$

text: So the two (straight-lines) $EA$, $AB$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $FD$, $DC$, respectively.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the two (straight-lines) $EA$, $AB$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $FD$, $DC$, respectively

text: And angle $FDC$ is equal to angle $EAB$, the external to the internal [Prop.~1.29].
Thus, the base $EB$ is equal to the base $FC$,

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the base $EB$ is equal to the base $FC$

text: and triangle $EAB$ will be equal to triangle $DFC$ [Prop.~1.4].

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: triangle $EAB$ will be equal to triangle $DFC$

text: Let $DGE$ have been taken away from both.
Thus, the remaining trapezium $ABGD$ is equal to the remaining trapezium $EGCF$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the remaining trapezium $ABGD$ is equal to the remaining trapezium $EGCF$

text: Let triangle $GBC$ have been added to both.
Thus, the whole parallelogram $ABCD$ is equal to the whole parallelogram $EBCF$.

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the whole parallelogram $ABCD$ is equal to the whole parallelogram $EBCF$

text: Thus, parallelograms which are on the same base and between the same parallels are equal to one another. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
